findings.source_quote: Οἱ δὲ ἐπιδεδωκότες τὰς ῥάβδους χλωράς, αὐτὰ δὲ τὰ ἄκρα ξηρὰ καὶ σχισμὰς ἔχοντα
findings.english_quote: The people whose rods were green, with dry and cracked tips
findings.issue: The simplified text omits the action of handing in the rods. The source identifies this group by the rods they submitted, not merely by rods they possessed. The same omission recurs in paragraph 3.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore the submission action in both descriptions, for example: “The people who handed in green rods with dry and cracked tips” and “The people who handed in their dry rods with only a little green.”

findings.source_quote: ἀλλ᾿ ἀκούσαντές μου τῶν ῥημάτων τὸ πλεῖστον μέρος ταχὺ μετενόησαν
findings.english_quote: Most heard my words and quickly repented.
findings.issue: Moving “most” before “heard” changes its scope. The source presents hearing the speaker’s words as the circumstance preceding the majority’s quick repentance; the English instead quantifies who heard as well as who repented. It also drops the explicit contrast introduced by ἀλλ᾿.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “But after hearing my words, most of them quickly repented.”

findings.source_quote: καὶ ἐγένετο ἡ κατοικία αὐτῶν εἰς τὸν πύργον.
findings.english_quote: Their dwelling was in the tower.
findings.issue: The static “was” loses the source’s assertion that their dwelling came to be in the tower following their repentance.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “And their dwelling came to be in the tower.”

summary: The standard reader text covers the selected Greek faithfully, but its theological metadata requires correction. Independent review of the simplified text finds omitted rod-submission actions, altered scope in the hearing-and-repentance clause, and loss of the dwelling’s transition, alongside inaccurate metadata. Both editions follow the servant and contextual repentance policies. The disclosed only-believed and suffering selections should remain; the supplied reports do not justify replacing them merely because alternatives exist. This review evaluates the selected source and supplied disclosures, not unseen manuscripts or exhaustive collation. Proposed corrections require fresh review.
